_headline: Two of the seven new nodes -- eurostat-suiot and eurostat-figaro -- give esa-2010 its first structurally distinct EU-to-EU dependency chain (SUIOT depends on ESA 2010 methodology; FIGARO depends on both SUIOT and ESA 2010), and esgab-annual-report is evidenced by a live, unbroken 17-year release listing (2009-2025), the cleanest cadence evidence any EU-branch node has had.
_open_questions: oecd-icio's cadence is not cleanly annual on the evidence in hand -- the OECD's own documentation names a '2023 edition' and a '2025 edition' two years apart, not a stated annual commitment. releases_per_year is set to 0.5 pending a clearer statement; do not treat this as confidently established the way eurostat-figaro's 'produced annually' claim is.

esac-opinion-work-programme -> eurostat-annual-work-programme is recorded with relationship_type 'cites', the closest available value, but ESAC's own language ('welcomes... underlines') is advisory commentary, not citation in the normal sense -- the same RelationshipType gap already flagged for ess-escb-mip-quality-report in eurosystem-ecb.json.

ess-peer-review-final-report's cadence (0.13/year, roughly once per 7-8 years) rests on three data points (2006-08, 2013-15, 2021-23) with an 8th round-based interval, the same generational-cadence treatment as esa-2010 and sna-2008 -- flagged, not silently treated as precise.
WIOD, EXIOBASE, EORA, GTAP-MRIO and OECD TiVA are named parallel global input-output databases in the GLOBAL-IO batch, none independently verified live this session -- see _dropped.

reports.title: Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables (SUIOTs)
reports.description: Matrices balancing supply and use of products across the economy to compile a single coherent GDP estimate. Eurostat's own page: 'Supply, use and input-output tables (SUIOTs) are matrices that provide a detailed picture of how goods and services are supplied and used in an economy.' Every country compiles its own SUIOTs and delivers them to Eurostat, which compiles the consolidated EU/euro-area version. Governed by the ESA 2010 transmission programme (Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/734).
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on Eurostat's own naio_10_n metadata page. Core tables (supply table, use table) are annual, delivered at t+36 months under the ESA 2010 transmission programme; a further set (use table at basic prices, margin tables, input-output tables) is delivered every 5 years (years ending in 0 or 5). releases_per_year reflects the annual core product.

entries.covers: Annual update of Supply and Use tables for the EU and euro area (FIGARO-based aggregate)

release_schedule.note: Eurostat does not publish a fixed-date release calendar entry for SUIOTs. National-level tables (naio_10_n) are published on a rolling/continuous basis throughout the year as individual countries transmit validated data (legal deadline: within 36 months after the end of the reference year, per the ESA 2010 transmission programme). The EU/euro-area consolidated aggregate (FIGARO-based), covered by the Statistics Explained article 'Supply and use tables for the European Union and the euro area', is updated once a year in autumn; the article itself states 'Data extracted: October 2025. Planned article update: October 2026', which is the closest thing to a stated next-release date and matches the corpus's releases_per_year=1.

reports.title: FIGARO — EU Inter-Country Supply, Use and Input-Output Tables
reports.publisher: Eurostat and the Joint Research Centre (JRC), European Commission
reports.description: 'Full International and Global Accounts for Research in Input-Output analysis.' The EU's inter-country supply, use and input-output tables, covering the 27 EU Member States, EFTA, EU candidate countries, 15 major trading partners and a 'Rest of the world' region, broken down by 64 products and industries. Eurostat's own page: 'The FIGARO tables have been developed by Eurostat and the Joint Research Centre of the European Commission (JRC). Since 2021, they are produced annually, covering the period from 2010 up to year T-2.'
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on Eurostat's own naio_10_fcp metadata page -- 'Since 2021, they are produced annually.'

entries.covers: 2027 FIGARO edition (inter-country supply, use and input-output tables, data series 2010-2025)

release_schedule.rule: Section 14.2 Punctuality (naio_10_fcp_esms.htm): 'There is no specific publication deadline. Eurostat usually releases the FIGARO data in July each year. However, the actual publication date may vary depending on the availability of input data and methodological developments.' Section 9 Frequency of dissemination: 'The FIGARO tables are released annually.'
release_schedule.note: The 2026 FIGARO edition has already been released (metadata page shows 'Metadata last certified/posted/update: 20 July 2026' and Section 14.1 Timeliness states 'The data release in 2026 consequently covers the period of 2010-2024'; Section 17.1 also describes 'The revision for the 2026 FIGARO edition'). So the next edition due is the 2027 release, expected around July 2027 per the publisher's stated (non-binding) punctuality pattern; exact date is announced only a few weeks ahead via Eurostat's release calendar (Section 8.1).

reports.title: OECD Inter-Country Input-Output (ICIO) Tables
reports.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
reports.description: A globally balanced view of inter-country and inter-industry flows of goods and services used as intermediate inputs and final demand. Built from national accounts main aggregates, SUTs/IOTs, balance of payments, and bilateral merchandise and services trade statistics for each country. OECD's own 2025-edition documentation: 'The new database covers all years from 1995 to 2022' -- an earlier-cited 2023 edition covered a shorter span. Reachable and confirmed current at oecd.org.
reports.cadence_note: NOT cleanly established as annual -- flagged in _open_questions. Two named editions in hand ('2023 edition', '2025 edition') are two years apart; releases_per_year of 0.5 is a placeholder pending a clearer statement of OECD's own release schedule.

entries.covers: Next (2027) edition of OECD ICIO tables / TiVA database, projected from the observed biennial-November pattern

release_schedule.note: Editions are launched jointly with the Trade in Value-Added (TiVA) database. Confirmed launch timing: 2021 edition launched 19 November 2021 (OECD-linked press coverage); 2023 edition materials published under the OECD path 'reports/2023/11/...' (November 2023); 2025 edition launched via OECD blog post dated 'blogs/2025/11/...' (November 2025). This gives three consecutive editions (2021, 2023, 2025) each released in November of an odd-numbered year, two years apart -- a consistent biennial-in-November pattern -- though OECD does not publish a forward release calendar or state a fixed rule committing to this cadence continuing.

reports.title: Annual Work Programme for European Statistics
reports.description: Annex IV to the Commission's annual financing decision for the Single Market Programme, implementing the SMP's European-statistics objective under Regulation (EU) 2021/690 and submitted to the Statistical System Committee under Article 17 of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009. The 2026 edition's own text: 'The 2026 WP will be the sixth one implementing the Single Market Programme 2021-2027.'
reports.cadence_note: Edition count stated directly by the document itself ('the sixth one'), the same evidentiary shape as ess-escb-mip-quality-report and esgab-annual-report.

entries.covers: Annual Work Programme for European Statistics 2027 (Commission Implementing Decision on financing / adopting the 2027 work programme)

release_schedule.note: Observed pattern: the Commission adopts the Annual Work Programme for European Statistics (as a Commission Implementing Decision on financing the Single Market Programme statistics strand and adopting the work programme) in mid-December of the year preceding the programme year. Confirmed data points: the 2020 work programme was adopted 13.12.2019 (C(2019) 8801 final, https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/10186/10309432/Financing-decision-2020_grant.pdf) and the 2026 work programme (matching the corpus's current PN1-2026.pdf) was adopted 18.12.2025 (C(2025) 8895 final, https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/10186/22849697/2026-financing-decision-smp.PDF). Separately, Article 17 of Regulation (EC) No 223/2009 (as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/759) states an earlier, distinct rule: 'The Commission shall submit to the ESS Committee its annual work programme by 30 April for the following year' -- this governs the consultation-stage submission of a draft programme to the European Statistical System Committee, not the final December adoption/publication date reflected in the entry above. Because the December adoption date is only observed (not stated as a fixed rule) and Eurostat's grants page did not expose a full year-by-year archive to WebFetch (JS-rendered 'Previous financing decisions' section), this is classified as observed-pattern rather than published-calendar or stated-rule.

reports.title: ESAC Opinion on the Draft Work Programme for European Statistics
reports.description: Annual advisory opinion by ESAC (established under Decision No 234/2008/EC) on the Commission's draft annual Work Programme for European Statistics, required by Article 2 of that Decision. Live-listed on ESAC's own opinions page with one dated entry per year.
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified on ESAC's own opinions page -- one Work Programme opinion per year, 2015 through 2026 confirmed by dated entries ('Opinion on the Draft 2027 Work Programme...(13 July 2026)' down to 'Opinion on Work Programme 2017 (1 March 2016)').

release_schedule.note: ESAC's opinions page lists no formal release calendar or statutory deadline for this opinion; the ESS Statistical Law (Reg. 223/2009) requires Eurostat to consult ESAC on the draft annual Work Programme but does not fix a date. Observed pattern: opinions on the following year's Draft Work Programme have been issued annually in late May-July (26 May 2020, 4 June 2021, 25 May 2022, 23 June 2023, 27 June 2024, 21 June 2025, 13 July 2026), i.e. roughly 6 months before the covered programme year begins. Next opinion (on the Draft 2028 Work Programme) is projected for ~mid-2027; exact date not published yet as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Final Report on the ESS Peer Reviews
reports.publisher: Eurostat, for the European Statistical System (ESS)
reports.description: Eurostat's consolidated final report to the European Parliament and Council on each round of ESS peer reviews against the European Statistics Code of Practice, covering every ESS member (NSIs and selected other national authorities) plus Eurostat itself (reviewed separately by ESGAB). Eurostat's own page: 'Eurostat prepared a final report on the third round of the European Statistical System peer reviews, which has been transmitted to the European Parliament and the Council.'
reports.cadence_note: Round-based, not annual -- three rounds confirmed live on Eurostat's own page: 2006-2008, 2013-2015, 2021-2023. Roughly once every 7-8 years; releases_per_year approximates the observed interval, same generational-cadence treatment as esa-2010 and sna-2008.

entries.covers: Final report/synthesis on first round of ESS peer reviews (round conducted 2006-2008)
Report to the European Parliament and Council on second round of ESS peer reviews (round conducted 2013-2015)
Final report on the third round of ESS peer reviews (round conducted 2021-2023), reference SWD(2024) 136, transmitted to the European Parliament and Council
Projected final report on a prospective fourth round of ESS peer reviews, if the observed ~7-9 year cadence between rounds continues

release_schedule.note: Eurostat's peer-review page (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/quality/peer-reviews/current-round-2021-2023) confirms three completed rounds: round 1 (2006-2008), round 2 (2013-2015), round 3 (2021-2023, final report SWD(2024)136 transmitted to the European Parliament and Council in 2024). No published calendar or explicit legal periodicity rule for a fourth round was found (multiple attempts to access the governing regulation, 223/2009 as amended by 2015/759, on EUR-Lex were blocked by an AWS WAF bot challenge returning empty/202 responses). The ~7-9 year gap between round starts (2006->2013->2021) and between final reports (~2008/09->~2015/16->2024) is irregular rather than a fixed cycle, so the projected 2031-2032 entry is a rough extrapolation with low confidence, not an announced date. No mention of a fourth round or its timing was found on any Eurostat peer-review subpage (first-round, second-round, third-round/current-round) as of 2026-08-11.

reports.title: Annual Report by the European Statistical Governance Advisory Board
reports.description: ESGAB's mandated annual report to the European Parliament and Council on the implementation of the European Statistics Code of Practice by Eurostat and the European Statistical System as a whole. Established by Decision No 235/2008/EC, Article 2(1): 'The Board's tasks shall be to: (a) prepare an annual report for the European Parliament and the Council on the implementation of the Code of Practice...' Individual reports self-identify by edition ('Sixteenth annual report', 'Seventeenth annual report').
reports.cadence_note: Live-verified two ways: Article 2(1) of the founding Decision (EUR-Lex) states the annual-report mandate verbatim; the ESGAB annual-reports landing page (ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/esgab/annual-reports) lists one dated report per year, unbroken, 2009 through 2025 -- 17 consecutive years.

release_schedule.note: ESGAB publishes one annual report per year but the publication date has been inconsistent over its history: earlier editions (e.g. 2018-2023 reports) were released January-March of the following year, while the two most recent editions (2024 report on 29 Oct 2024, 2025 report on 11 Nov 2025) shifted to October/November of the same year. No official calendar or stated statutory deadline was found on the publisher's page (https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/web/esgab/annual-reports); the projected next entry extrapolates from the most recent two-year Oct/Nov clustering, not a fixed rule, so confidence is only medium.

dependencies.basis: Eurostat's own metadata page: 'SUIOTs follow the statistical concepts and definitions of the European System of Accounts - ESA 2010 as implemented through Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 and amended by Regulation (EU) 2023/734.' Live-verified 2026-08-05.
Eurostat's own metadata page: 'The compilation of FIGARO tables relies on several data sources, including: National supply and use tables...' Live-verified 2026-08-05.
'The methodology underlying the FIGARO tables corresponds to the "European Systems of Accounts 2010" (ESA 2010) methodology.'

ESAC's 2026 opinion: 'ESAC welcomes the ambitious 2026 draft Work Programme for European statistics which will be the 6th Annual Work Programme under the Single Market Programme 2021-2027.' relationship_type 'cites' is the closest available value -- ESAC advises on/reviews the Work Programme rather than using its data or deriving from its methodology; flagged in _open_questions as an imperfect fit, the same gap already logged for ess-escb-mip-quality-report.

_dropped.why: A soft-law instrument (replacing Recommendation 2009/498/EC) inviting Member States to apply the Single Integrated Metadata Structure (SIMS). Not itself a recurrently published document -- it is a one-off legal act, same category as the Eurosystem collateral Guidelines excluded in G.43.md. Already recorded as context in PartB_soft_connections_2026-08-04.md (sc-02, sc-04, sc-05); no new node.

_dropped.edge: [WIOD / EXIOBASE / EORA / GTAP-MRIO / OECD TiVA] -> node
_dropped.why: Named as parallel global multi-regional input-output databases in the GLOBAL-IO batch, each with a plausible title, but none independently verified live this session -- WIOD's own cited update ('recently updated to 2014', from a document written c. 2019) reads as possibly discontinued rather than confirmed recurring. Filed as leads, not chased further.

The Work Programme names its own legal basis explicitly (Reg. 2021/690 Annex II, Reg. 223/2009 Article 17), but neither regulation is itself a node in this corpus -- both are legal-spine instruments, same category as the EBS Regulation and Regulation 223/2009 already excluded elsewhere in the branch.

ESGAB conducts Eurostat's own peer review within the third-round process ('Eurostat's peer review was carried out by ESGAB'), but this is ESGAB acting as reviewer for one ESS member's review, not a citation between the two published report series. Not the same relationship as an edge between the two documents' own content -- no edge minted.
